summary: A 1912 state plan for a wireless fire lookout on Equinox Mountain; later lists mark it removed, and the summit now has a toll road and broadcast towers.

facts.status_note: Listed as removed. The summit is now reached by a private toll road that passes broadcast towers.

events.note: Planned lookout station with wireless reporting; the state report calls the scheme experimental

evidence.supports: 1912 plan for a lookout station on Equinox Mountain equipped with wireless
evidence.quote: Arrangements have been made to establish a lookout station for the summer of 1912 on Equinox Mountain equipped with wireless.

evidence.supports: fourth annual report of the Vermont state forester
evidence.quote: 4th Annual Report of the Vermont State Forester

evidence.supports: fires reported by wireless to a base station, operator telephones the warden
evidence.quote: Fires will be reported by wireless to a base station where the operator will telephone to the warden in the town where the fire is located.

evidence.supports: scheme largely experimental, government money, hoped to be cheaper than telephone lines
evidence.quote: This is largely experimental and is carried on with Government money in the hope that this method of reporting fires will prove workable and prove more economical than building telephone lines throughout forest regions.

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts page status word Removed
Vermont list marks Equinox tower gone; Bennington County
evidence.quote: Equinox Mountain Bennington 43.16594 -73.11715 Open Tower Gone

evidence.supports: Equinox is the highest peak of the Taconic Range
evidence.quote: Equinox Mountain is the highest peak of the Taconic Range

evidence.supports: rises nearly 3,000 feet above eastern footings in Manchester
evidence.quote: It rises nearly 3,000 feet (914 meters) above its eastern footings in Manchester

evidence.supports: summit reached by private toll road to observation building, past broadcast towers
evidence.quote: A summit observation building is reached via a privately operated toll road, which passes near various towers used for broadcast and other purposes.

corrections.why: The Vermont list on firelookout.org gives Tower for Equinox Mountain, and no source we read says platform. Needs a human check.

notes_for_editor: One 1912 state report plans a wireless lookout here. No source we read says it opened, who staffed it, or what structure stood on the summit. Killington Peak appears in a search snippet as the 1912 wireless site; not read, not used. The FFLA list writes Open before Tower; meaning unclear, not used. The kind correction is for human review. Summit description is from Wikipedia; no site visit.
